deviations.claim_in_article: “Through Muse, trained human contract workers made some calls and completed the exchanges with users.”
deviations.issue: The Ledger supports staff completing calls with the other party, including businesses or stores, but does not say they completed exchanges with Muse users. The English article changes the identity of the party on the other end of the call.
deviations.explanation: “Some calls” is consistent with the Ledger, but substituting “users” for the call counterpart changes the participant and the scope of the interaction; the claim about exchanges with Muse users is unsupported.

deviations.claim_in_article: “When AI struggled, a person could help.”
deviations.issue: The Ledger confirms that trained human contractors made some calls, but does not establish that a person was brought in when Muse struggled or that this was the test’s operating model.
deviations.explanation: The conditional role of a human as support when AI struggles is not in the Ledger; “could” softens the statement but does not establish that operating model.

deviations.claim_in_article: “An AI called. That was what people thought as they spoke” and “people who thought they were speaking with AI were actually speaking with human staff.”
deviations.issue: The Ledger reports inadequate disclosure during the human-concierge test, but does not establish that the people receiving the calls believed they were speaking with AI.
deviations.explanation: The recipients’ belief is asserted as fact, while the Ledger establishes lack of appropriate disclosure, not what recipients thought.

deviations.claim_in_article: “One helper meant one more person handling private data.”
deviations.issue: This states that a helper actually handled private data, whereas the Ledger records employees’ concern that sensitive information might be shared with contract staff.
deviations.explanation: The article turns a reported possibility and privacy concern into a definite instance of data handling. The nearby “might be shared” does not make this categorical follow-up consistent with the Ledger.
deviations.qualifier_text: “the user’s sensitive information might be shared with contract workers at a call center”
